clue.text: Unusual comment on backward island

parts.note: a comment is a remark

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the island's name from right to left

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A strange observation about an island that is behind the times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' reads ELBA right to left, so 'comment' is followed by a word meaning capable rather than an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the ordinary is worthy of notice, hence unusual.

clue.text: Odd criterion of stability!

parts.note: the word for a byword of firmness is also a verb for swaying to and fro, which is why the measure is odd

explanation.surface: A strange way of measuring how steady something is.
explanation.walkthrough: A thing 'solid as a rock' is the image of steadiness, yet to rock is to sway unsteadily: hence 'odd'.
explanation.definitionFit: A boulder is the proverbial image of something immovable, while the verb means to wobble.

clue.text: Sounds like a man of letters

indicators.note: signals that the word for a man is to be heard, not spelt, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: Someone sounds like a literary figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of letters' suggests a writer, but 'letters' alone is the definition, with 'of' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Post delivered by the postman consists of letters.

clue.text: Remembering about service contributions

parts.note: re is a short word meaning about or concerning
the collection is the money given during a church service

explanation.surface: Recalling what was put in the plate at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A memory brought back to mind is an act of remembering.

clue.text: A poisonous summer ?

explanation.surface: A toxic hot season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is read as one who sums, not the season; 'A poisonous' stands for a venomous snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The viper is Britain's venomous snake; someone who adds up figures is literally one who sums.

clue.text: Archbishop leads trip in mountains

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury in the 1930s

indicators.note: to trip is to stumble, so the letters of the next word fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A senior churchman guides a hiking expedition in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' looks like an outing but rearranges LEADS into DALES. The Langdales are fells in the English Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: The Langdale Pikes are a group of fells in Cumbria's Lake District.

clue.text: Whip round ?

explanation.surface: A collection taken from colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip round' is a British collection of money; split, it gives two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: To whip is to thrash; a police officer's regular patrol route is his round.

clue.text: Battle brings member into ring ?

explanation.surface: A fight puts a club member into the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition describes betrothal, when a ring is given to the partner-to-be.
explanation.definitionFit: A clash of armies is a military fight; a betrothal is marked with a ring.

clue.text: These maids are employed in a river locality

indicators.note: the letters are put to use in a new arrangement, the setter's sign to rearrange them

explanation.surface: Domestic servants find work in a riverside district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are employed' signals rearranging THESE MAIDS.
explanation.definitionFit: The banks of London's main river form a district named after it.

clue.text: Agreeing to give money to detectives in note form

parts.note: to coin money is to mint it
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
G is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Consenting to pay the police in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of British police; 'form' and the two 'to's are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that coincide are in agreement or occur together.

clue.text: Some fear gangster's return in the city

indicators.note: return means the concealed letters are read in the opposite direction
only some of the letters of the words are used, a sign of letters concealed in them

explanation.surface: A city where people dread a mobster coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' finds ARGA in feAR GAngster; 'return' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Removal by ship?

parts.note: the weight of water a vessel pushes aside is its measure, so moving water out of the way is a removal done by a ship

explanation.surface: Moving house by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests shipping furniture; a ship's tonnage is measured by the water it pushes aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's tonnage is the weight of water it pushes aside, and the general word also means moving something from its place.

clue.text: Dickensian's trifling little poem by Tennyson

parts.note: Alfred was Lord Tennyson's first name
a jingle is a slight piece of catchy verse

explanation.surface: A slight verse from Tennyson inspired by Dickens.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Alfred Jingle is the strolling actor in Dickens's Pickwick Papers; 'by' sets the poem next to the poet's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr Jingle is a character in Pickwick Papers, so he is a figure from Dickens.

clue.text: The thing is to hold on to protests

parts.note: an object is a thing

indicators.note: the word is is made to hold the next word inside it

explanation.surface: The point is to keep going with complaints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hold' makes IS enclose ON. 'The thing is' reads like the start of a sentence but is two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaints raised against something are protests.

clue.text: Perhaps a hunter has occasion to accompany a custodian

parts.note: an occasion is a time
a custodian is a keeper

explanation.surface: A huntsman gets a chance to go out with a gamekeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: A hunter is a pocket watch with a hinged cover, not a huntsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunter watch is one example of a device for telling the hour.

clue.text: Good news for groom in prison

parts.note: the woman for a groom is his bride
well means good, as in all is well

explanation.surface: The groom hears happy news in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a bulletin, 'bride well' is good news for a groom. Bridewell was a London house of correction, hence any prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridewell, an old London jail, gave its name to houses of correction generally.

clue.text: With current circulation notes have to be changed at sea

parts.note: an eddy is water circling against the main current

indicators.note: the letters of the word must be changed round into a new order

explanation.surface: Banknotes need exchanging on a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'have to be changed' rearranges NOTES into STONE. The Eddystone rocks, with their lighthouse, lie in the English Channel off Plymouth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eddystone reef and lighthouse stand out in open water south-west of Plymouth.

clue.text: Animals turn up by degrees

indicators.note: turn tells us the following short word is turned round

parts.note: MAs are Master of Arts degrees

explanation.surface: Creatures appear gradually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by degrees' looks like 'gradually'; 'turn' reverses UP to PU, and MAS are university degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumas are big cats of the Americas.

clue.text: Leave the river army in retreat

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: an army retreating goes backwards, so its letters are reversed

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: Troops abandon the riverbank as they fall back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retreat' turns TA into AT. An exeat is a school's formal permission to be absent.
explanation.definitionFit: An exeat is permission to be absent, as from a college or school.

clue.text: Took certain courses about said members being scorned

annotationWithheld.why: Took certain courses about said members being scorned (9): DINED around SDAI or ISDA, an anagram of SAID, but no word signals the anagram unless 'about' serves as both container and anagram indicator; 'certain' and 'members' are unexplained.
annotationWithheld.clue: Took certain courses about said members being scorned

clue.text: Article owned by Dostoevsky

parts.note: the is the definite article
owned means possessed

explanation.surface: Something belonging to the Russian novelist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by Dostoevsky' defines one of his novels, also known in English as Demons.
explanation.definitionFit: Dostoevsky's 1872 novel about revolutionaries is known under this English title.

clue.text: Minister to initiate court action ?

explanation.surface: A government minister begins legal proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' can be a tennis court, where play starts with a serve, or a law court, where a writ is served.
explanation.definitionFit: To minister to someone is to attend them; tennis play and legal writs both begin with this act.

clue.text: U.S. settler from obscure quarter

parts.note: dim means obscure or faint
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An American pioneer from a remote district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settler' is not a pioneer but something that settles a bill: an American coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The ten-cent coin of the United States can be used to pay, or settle, a debt.

clue.text: Female of note ?

explanation.surface: A woman of distinction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of note' suggests fame; split, a chit is a pert young woman and also a short written note.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheeky young girl is called a chit, and so is a brief memo or voucher.

clue.text: Give up attempt to back secret police

indicators.note: to back is to go backwards, so the joined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: taken from give up
to have a go is to make an attempt

explanation.surface: Abandoning an effort to support the secret police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to back' turns UPGO around. The OGPU was the Soviet secret police of the 1920s and 30s.
explanation.definitionFit: The OGPU was the Soviet state security service between 1923 and 1934.

clue.text: Company is a fresh organization — possible catch in this !

indicators.note: organization means the letters are reorganized into a new order

explanation.surface: A firm made up of fishing enthusiasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organization' reworks IS A FRESH. Coarse fish are freshwater fish other than salmon and trout, so 'possible catch' is fair; 'in this' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Roach, carp and pike are freshwater species an angler might land.

clue.text: The good one is so kind !

explanation.surface: A good person is so considerate.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'good sort' is a decent person, and the same word means a kind or type.
explanation.definitionFit: A decent person is a good sort; type and kind are synonyms of it.

clue.text: Possibly ten people among the others show indignation

indicators.note: among puts the following pieces inside the word for the others

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may be arranged in another order

parts.note: men are people

explanation.surface: Perhaps ten folk in the crowd are angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' makes ENT from TEN; 'among' places that and MEN inside REST. 'show' is a link to the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter anger at unfair treatment is indignation.
